html:
"The Sad Night": the flight of the Spanish and their allies from Tenochtitlan on the night of 30 June 1520, with heavy losses.

After the toxcatl-massacre the city was in revolt. Moctezuma was dead, and the Mexica chose a new ruler, Cuitlahuac. Cortes decided to slip out at night along the Tacuba causeway. Mexica warriors found them and attacked from canoes and from the road, where bridges had been cut. Many Spaniards drowned, weighed down by stolen gold. The Spanish lost several hundred men, and many more of their allies from Tlaxcala died.

Cortes is said to have wept under a tree on the road. The survivors fought off the Mexica at Otumba and fell back to Tlaxcala.

It was a defeat, but not the end. Smallpox soon hit the city and killed Cuitlahuac. Cortes returned with Tlaxcalan help and new ships, leading to the fall of Tenochtitlan in 1521.
sum: "The Sad Night": the flight of the Spanish and their allies from Tenochtitlan on the night of 30 June 1520, with heavy losses.
